evidence: src/infrastructure/http/RequestReader.ts: requiredString delegates to optionalString, and both throw BadRequestError, so the field validation rule lives in one place
src/infrastructure/http/middleware/errorHandler.ts: STATUS_BY_KIND and the `err instanceof BadRequestError` branch are the only place errors are turned into HTTP status codes
src/infrastructure/http/BadRequestError.ts: one HTTP-level error type, used by both RequestReader and errorHandler
src/infrastructure/http/createApp.ts: createApp builds the Express app, mounts the routes, adds a 404 fallback and installs errorHandler last
Minor: the 404 fallback in createApp.ts writes `{ error: 'Route not found' }` directly, repeating the response shape that errorHandler.ts also builds
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All four files deal with one concern: the Express HTTP adapter. createApp.ts wires up the app. RequestReader.ts parses request bodies and throws the module's own BadRequestError. errorHandler.ts turns DomainError, BadRequestError and malformed-JSON errors into HTTP responses. Each rule lives in one place. Field type and required checks are only in RequestReader (requiredString builds on optionalString). The mapping from errors to status codes is only in errorHandler (STATUS_BY_KIND plus the BadRequestError branch). Nothing goes around the module's own pieces. RequestReader reports problems through BadRequestError, and errorHandler is the only place that handles it. One small point: createApp's inline 404 handler builds the `{ error: ... }` response body itself instead of going through errorHandler. That means two files build the same error response shape. It is a minor overlap, not a split or a misplaced invariant, so the unit passes.
